standard_prerequisites.name: The Yoneda lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the representing object in the hypothesis is unique up to unique isomorphism and provides the identities used throughout.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sheaves as coequalizers of coproducts of representables
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the coequalizer presentation of an arbitrary sheaf by coproducts of representable sheaves, using that the chosen family of objects covers.

core_obligations: The representing objects and the maps into them (proof lines 5282-5309): by Yoneda the sheaf representing the values of the pullback is unique up to unique isomorphism, the map corresponding to the identity exhibits the bijection of the hypothesis as composition with it, and the author defines the action of the sought functor on the representable sheaves by the characterizing identity, showing compatibility with composition directly from it.
Coproducts (proof lines 5312-5322): the product of the bijections for a family extends the functor to coproducts of representable sheaves.

Arbitrary sheaves (proof lines 5324-5371): using that the chosen objects cover, an arbitrary sheaf is presented as a coequalizer of coproducts of representable sheaves; the author defines the value of the functor on it by the corresponding coequalizer and verifies the adjunction by an explicit chain of identifications of morphism sets through the coequalizer and the defining bijections.
proof_roadmap: Use Yoneda to produce the representing sheaves and define the functor on representables by the characterizing identity.
Extend the definition to coproducts of representables by taking products of the bijections.
Present an arbitrary sheaf as a coequalizer of such coproducts and verify the adjunction by computing morphism sets.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a left adjoint for the pullback of a morphism of topoi under two hypotheses: that the values of the pullback on a chosen family of objects are represented by sheaves, functorially, and that every object has a covering by members of that family (statement lines 5266-5279). The proof is a complete construction: Yoneda produces the representing sheaves and exhibits the given bijection as composition with a canonical map, from which the author defines the functor on representables (proof lines 5282-5309); the definition is extended to coproducts of representables (proof lines 5312-5322); and an arbitrary sheaf is presented as a coequalizer of such coproducts, on which the functor is defined by the induced coequalizer, with the adjunction verified by a chain of identifications of morphism sets (proof lines 5324-5371). The non-formal content is the definition on representables and the adjunction verification. The claim is H2: a construction carried out in three stages with every input named.
